texts.facts: 3. Brief facts of the case leading to this appeal are that the petitioners filed petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1998 seeking compensation of Rs.1,25,00,000/- for death of Vinuth in the accident. Respondent No.2 filed objections. The respondent no.2 has no knowledge about the relationship between the deceased and the petitioners and the compensation claimed is very exorbitant. It is also contended that the legality, validity and authenticity of the alleged qualification and certified are not from notified and recognised educational institutions and the deceased had no income as on the date of the accident. Further, the driver who was driving the vehicle at the alleged NC: 2024:KHC-D:8313-DB time of accident did not possess, legal, valid and effective driving licence and the owner, knowingly, violated the conditions of the insurance policy. The Tribunal allowed the claim petition by holding that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the bus by its driver and awarded compensation of Rs.12,70,000/-.
texts.arguments: The Tribunal failed to note that the deceased was aged 24 years as on the date of accident and was hale and healthy. To substantiate the submissions, the learned counsel relied upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of RAJWATI @ RAJJO AND OTHERS NC: 2024:KHC-D:8313-DB v. UNITED INDIA INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED AND OTHERS reported in (2023) ACR 183 (SC) and the decision of this Court in the case of MANAGER, RELIANCE GENERAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. v. SHIVALEELA AND OTHERS reported in 2020 ACJ 2421.

18. In view of Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the function of the Tribunal or Court is to award "just compensation".
The Motor Vehicle Act is beneficial and welfare legislation.
A "just compensation" is one which is reasonable on the basis of the evidence produced on record.
It cannot be said to have become time-barred.
There is no need for new cause of action to claim an enhanced amount.

The courts are duty- bound to award just compensation as observed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of RAMLA v. NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMTED reported in Smt. Shaila W/O Manjappa K.D vs The Managing Director on 21 June, 2024 Indi
